unavailable_fields.per_collective_comm_bytes_and_wire_time: Single-device inference runs no collectives; device_telemetry exposes only device-wide NVML PCIe rates with native sampling windows, not per-collective bytes; PCIe/NVLink traffic must not be inferred from logical payload or memcpy sizes.
unavailable_fields.gradient_bucket_links: coverage.json reports 0 backward_associated_kernels and 0 autograd_ranges for this inference-only workload; exact bucket links require native correlation plus observed gradient-storage membership, so no bucket candidates exist to confirm or disambiguate.
unavailable_fields.peak_reserved_bytes_and_allocator_segmen: No collector in available-collectors.json exposes torch caching-allocator reserved/segment snapshots; the frozen objective is peak_allocated_bytes, which the source already measures directly via torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() after reset_peak_memory_stats().
unavailable_fields.clean_host_dispatch_costs: python_runtime runs a separate warmed cProfile that perturbs execution; its inclusive/self times are not clean performance scores or GPU compute durations, and host dispatch is outside the frozen memory objective (the throughput constraint is measured cleanly by the paired-repeat harness).
unavailable_fields.gpu_readiness_and_consumer_completion_bo: execution_timeline reports clock alignment bounds for matching CPU submissions only, and GPU readiness/consumer completion may remain unknown; not selected because kernel-to-op association is already complete (123/123) and it never determines subsequent search actions.

plan.rationale: Single-device ResNet-18 FP32 inference; frozen objective is minimize peak_allocated_bytes subject to images_per_second >= 0.95x baseline with logits/top1 fidelity (atol/rtol 1e-4, exact top1). The source measures the objective directly (torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats + max_memory_allocated around a synchronized infer), so the remaining diagnostic need is candidate evaluation plus device-level corroboration, not new attribution. torch already ran and coverage is complete (coverage.json: 123/123 cuda_kernels associated, 0 unassociated, 0 root_only, 0 backward_associated, 0 autograd_ranges, 0 ambiguous_forward_sequences), and the workload is plain eager inference with no CUDA graphs, so no overlap, graph-tracing or attribution question remains for which nsys would add value. candidate_diagnostics is selected as the primary collector: it runs candidate memory reductions (preserving source dtype, TF32 policy, seed, real data and completion boundaries) in the leased worker and reports their peak_allocated_bytes, images_per_second and logits/top1 against the constraint. device_telemetry is selected narrowly for NVML memory and utilization samples to corroborate that allocated-byte reductions appear at the device level and that candidates do not leave the device idle; these are device-wide readings with native windows, carry no per-op or per-collective byte attribution, and PCIe rates are deliberately not requested because inputs are GPU-resident and model loading is outside the declared workload boundary. Excluded: nsys (no remaining attribution/overlap/graph question; it cannot by itself separate NCCL waiting from wire transfer or prove bucket identity, and there is no NCCL here); collective_calibration (communication capability is not_applicable for a single-device task; a synthetic full-world SUM allreduce reference experiment with correctness checks has no bearing on this objective and is not a performance lower bound or critical-path estimate); execution_timeline (no CPU-submit/synchronization attribution gaps, inference has no gradient post-accumulate callbacks, and it is passive evidence that never replaces a communication hook or determines search actions); python_runtime (host dispatch/binding costs are not the objective, cProfile perturbs execution, and its times are not clean performance scores or GPU compute durations); torch (already ran with full kernel association, so re-running adds nothing).
